newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CSFB to revamp Russia fund business.
newsitem.headline: CSFB to revamp Russia fund business.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB) plans to revamp of its Moscow fund activities after having run into a number of difficulties in the Russian capital including property lease problems and the loss of two key managers.
CSFB has layed off some 50 employees at the Moscow operation and now intends to sell funds through partnerships with Russia-based banks, CSFB spokesman Paul Rhyn said.

CSFB in January announced the launch of three funds -- a Rouble money market fund, a hard currency money market fund and a large capitalisation equity fund -- it planned to offer to the Russian public.
But according to an article in the Swiss daily Tages Anzeiger, fund sales volume thus far, at some $15.5 million, were far below expectations.
Rhyn said he did not know exactly what kind of targets were set or the volume of business done to date. But he did say that CSFB had most likely not met the targets set for the Russian business.
He also said differences with regard to lease contracts on properties occupied in Moscow led to CSFB vacating the facilities about a month ago. He declined to provide specifics.

About a month ago Urs Haener, who co-managed the business in Russia with Alexander Knaster of the U.S., left the company and more recently Bernhard Steiner, a top manager in the operation's credit and market risk management department, also departed. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
